narrative:

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your total years of experience across all jobs, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here, and the relatively short time you have spent in your current role. 

Your 6–10 years of overall experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1–5 years of total experience, your mid-level tenure aligns more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having received external job opportunities during your time here was a strong signal in the same direction; most employees who stay never receive such offers. Your 1–5 years in this specific organization also contributed to the “will leave” outcome, as shorter current tenure is more common among those who depart than among those who remain.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture for the model that you are likely to leave. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring whether improved recognition, better work-life support, or clearer promotion paths could change your outlook. You may also want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your long-term plans.
